title: DXF-only peer lineages and projection boundaries
mode: deeper/broader primary-source research and plan refinement
scope: Screen DXF-only parser and callback-library routes not represented in the latest peer matrix
Distinguish document preservation from callback/projection APIs
Check lineage between the JavaScript dxf-parser and its Python port
Refine optional comparator admission without adding recurring validation work

sources.project: QCAD dxflib programmer guide and feature page
sources.observation: The guide says dxflib invokes consumer callbacks and does not retain entities/document information. Its feature page lists selected DXF entity/object families and documents R15 (AutoCAD 2000) as the writer version. Explicit 3DFACE/SOLID/TRACE class coverage is not ACIS/ACDS B-rep support.

The JavaScript project parses DXF text into a JavaScript object, reports support for most 2D entities and selected document structures, and explicitly lists 3DSolids and some less-common entities/objects as unsupported. The reviewed API is a parser/projection, not a writer or raw-byte-preservation contract.

The package describes itself as ASCII-DXF-only, alpha, and compatible with the output structure of the JavaScript dxf-parser; it explicitly attributes inspiration to that project. PyPI reports a release on 2026-09-03. These are one related schema/output lineage, not two independent parser votes.

sources.project: BRL-CAD DXF converter guide and GCV architecture documentation
sources.observation: BRL-CAD documents dxf-g as conversion into its own geometry database and says the historical DXF importer predates ACIS support. GCV converts through an in-memory BRL-CAD database and warns source objects may lack a direct analogous target primitive; this is a geometry projection, not a document roundtrip.

planImpact.implementationSummary: Added a narrow DXF-only comparator screen for dxflib, JavaScript/Python dxf-parser, and the BRL-CAD conversion boundary. Clarified callback/projection versus retained-document preservation, ASCII/version limits, and shared parser lineage. No local codec defect or new implementation item was identified.
